# Camera transitions

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Cuts the camera makes: whips, snap zooms, zoom-throughs, dives and moves carried across the seam. 18 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Line leaves upward as the next rises from below

`dv-vertical-carousel-handover` · transitions · workhorse · energy calm · any

A finished line or status accelerates upward (with a little vertical blur) and leaves, while the next line or list rises from below, blurred, and eases into place: the reading direction becomes the motion.

- **Build:** Words exit 'launch' upward + the next Words rising with focusIn. Anatomy: Exit ease-in 2 -> 19 px/f; entry rise 83 px blurred, easing 8-16 f. Sound: A punchy hit on the arrival.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Exit 20 f; entry 16-20 f; overlap 4-6 f.
- **Use when:** Sequences of statements or status steps.
- **Avoid when:** Both lines on screen and sharp at once.

### Exit at speed into a dark frame, next world fades up

`dv-whip-to-dark-frame` · transitions · accent · energy medium · any

The outgoing shot accelerates away (an orbit ramping into a 3-frame whip, an assembly flying off, a pull-out that darkens, a last line pushing in while the floor glow sinks, a logo drifting back as it fades) into one or two dark frames, and the next world fades up from them in a few frames.

- **Build:** blackDipState({ cut, black: 2, fadeUp: 8 }) after an exit on E.launchIn. Anatomy: Exit ease-in to 15 %/f or 308 px/f; 1-2 black frames; fade-up about 10 f. Sound: A beat on the black (+2 ms); a music gap begins; sub-bass under the glow.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.blackDipState`
- **Timing:** Exit 18-50 f; black 2-5 f at 60; fade-up 8-10 f.
- **Use when:** Changing worlds; before the end card.
- **Avoid when:** Long blacks (over 2 frames at 24-30 fps).

### Old layout whips out, new layout whips in from the same side

`dv-counter-whip-swap` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

The old composition accelerates out to the right and the new one arrives from the right moving left, decelerating: a swap that reverses direction at the cut.

- **Build:** Two whips with opposite directions; declare the seam as a position seam (not velocity). Anatomy: Out quad-in to 110 px/f; in cubic-out. Sound: An onset 48 ms after the cut.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Out 30 f, in 42 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** Comparing two states (before / after, old / new).
- **Avoid when:** Using it as the default (it breaks velocity matching on purpose).

### Snap back from a giant word to the full line

`dv-snap-back-to-wide` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

From a giant first word (or a line panning off the edge while it types), a hard cut to the full line at about 36-97 % of the scale, landing slightly small and blurred and growing to rest as the defocus clears.

- **Build:** punchOut-style cut with scaleBreath mode 'same' (open 0.97) and a short defocus. Anatomy: Cut lands at 0.974 scale, grows 6 f; defocus clears; the pan before runs on an expo-in. Sound: A speech hit 2 f before the cut.
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom`
- **Timing:** 1 f + 12 f at 60 fps; pans 56 f.
- **Use when:** Revealing the whole sentence after a close-up word.
- **Avoid when:** Landing exactly at rest (the slight undersize carries the motion).

### Zoom cut through a dither dissolve

`dv-dither-zoom-cut` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Between two frames a globe jumps from one size to 3.4x larger through a 3-frame pixel-dither dissolve, then the view tilts on an expo-out.

- **Build:** A static seeded dither mask plate stepped in three thresholds (HardStep) between the two shots. Anatomy: Scale jump on the cut; seeded dither mask dissolving over 3 f. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Pixel.Pixelate`
- **Timing:** Cut 1 f + dither 8 f; tilt 35 f.
- **Use when:** Zooming into a planet, a map, an image.
- **Avoid when:** Fine-detail subjects (the dither eats them).

### Camera passes through a ring of cards

`dv-through-the-ring` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A ring of cards seen down its axis: thin radial slivers grow in from the frame edges and thicken (tints first, then real thumbnails); the camera rises and pushes through the ring, the arch of cards sweeps out of frame, and the first word is already there on the other side.

- **Build:** Cards on a 3D ring (rotateY per card, translateZ radius) with the camera's pitch and k. Anatomy: Slivers coverage 1 -> 37 %; push with vertical flow 2 -> 43 px/f; sweep 13 f; word 20 f expo-out. Sound: A chat pop; a sub-drop as the camera exits the ring. Materials: The ring's cards arrive as needle-like spikes radiating from the frame edges in a two-hue gradient (outer warm, inner deep), pure colour for 12 f; as they widen they reveal video cards seen edge-on, still tinted (colour blend, opacity = 1 - width), and the tint drains in 8 f to true colour.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Materials:** The ring's cards arrive as needle-like spikes radiating from the frame edges in a two-hue gradient (outer warm, inner deep), pure colour for 12 f; as they widen they reveal video cards seen edge-on, still tinted (colour blend, opacity = 1 - width), and the tint drains in 8 f to true colour.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Slivers 28 f; push 60 f.
- **Use when:** A gallery of examples as a portal.
- **Avoid when:** Flat rings (it needs the perspective).

### Dive through a soft layer

`tr-dive-through-layer` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature · also `dv-dive-through-layer`

A soft foreground layer (mist, a frosted panel, a cloud bank) rises while the scene behind defocuses and travels up; for a few frames there is only the soft layer, the cut hides there, and the next subject rises out of it with its focus racking a beat behind its position.

- **Build:** <Dive frame start outgoing background incoming occluder={<Img src=plate />} />: a static plate with soft edges, never an animated blur radius.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Dive.Dive`, `fx/Dive.diveState`
- **Timing:** Rise 40 f (ease-in), defocus to 16 px at 1080p, 12 f fully covered (the cut in the middle), clear 20 f; the subject rises 0.12 of the height over 18 f and racks from 14 px over 36 f, starting 4 f after it moves.
- **Use when:** Moving from a statement into a product shot; a depth change.
- **Avoid when:** Flat graphic films with no depth planes.

### Flash cut inside a whip

`tr-flash-cut-whip` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, vertical

The camera whips on an ease-in that never brakes; one over-exposed frame with a faint ghost, one dark frame of horizontal streaks, and the next shot is already sliding in and pulls back as it lands.

- **Build:** <FlashCut frame cut whip={{ dir }} slide pull out in />; put the swell's peak on the flash frame. The whip's tail and the slide's head carry the whip-shutter streak (smear 'draw', house: DirBlur at 360 degrees); smear 'shutter' declares those frames as camera blur for the finishing pass instead. Declare the flash (declares()).
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.FlashCut`, `fx/CutFx.flashCutState`
- **Timing:** Whip 24 f on E.launchIn over 0.24 of the frame width (fastest on its last frame); flash 1 f at about 92 % white with a 0.3 ghost; streak 1 f; slide 28 f on E.snapOut from 0.55 of the width, opening at several times the whip's last speed, so its first frames are the most smeared of the cut and it sharpens as it lands; pull 28 f to 0.65 on E.glideOut.
- **Use when:** A fast camera move between two parts of the product; the energetic join of a launch film.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films with no whips; more than once a film.

### One jump frame hides the cut inside a zoom

`dv-jump-frame-hidden-cut` · transitions · signature · energy high · any

A zoom builds on an exponential ease-in, then ONE frame carries a huge scale step (+30-52 %, or 71-86 % of the log move) where the cut hides, often with a brightness flash; the move then eases out in the new shot (a zoom into the input where the typed text jumps ahead; an app pulling back into a wall of app tiles).

- **Build:** <SnapZoom pre post flash={{ gain }}> with the content swap on the jump frame. Anatomy: Ease-in 0.1 -> 3.7-16 %/f, the jump frame (with a +61 % luma flash optional), ease-out 11-30 f. Sound: An onset on the jump; a pop and a sub on the switch.
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom`
- **Timing:** Build 16-20 f; jump 1 f; land 20-30 f.
- **Use when:** Hiding a cut or a content jump in a camera event.
- **Avoid when:** More than one jump frame in a move.

### Portal zoom with aspect morph

`tr-portal-aspect-zoom` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, feature

A window opens in the middle of a solid tile. Tile and window grow faster and faster while the square stretches to 16:9, until the window's interior is the next scene and the tile's border has flown off the edges.

- **Build:** Draw an outer rect in the accent and an inner rect inset by 30% of the outer width and height on each side. The next scene renders inside the inner rect's clip (insetClip) from frame 0, at its final transform. Outer width w = lmix(204, 4800, prog(f, 0, 39, E.linear)), a pure exponential of about ×1.084 per frame, with aspect = mix(1, 16/9, prog(f, 0, 30, E.smooth)) and height = w / aspect. The accent border's outer edges leave the frame near frame 30, and the inner window covers the frame at frame 39, when the clip is dropped. Optional lead-in: the words on either side speed inward under the tile (translateX by their distance over 22 f on E.in, with blurOut). Then the tile turns 90 deg like a cube to bring a plain accent face to the front (CSS 3D box, front = the mark, side = accent at brightness 0.85, over 12 f on E.inOut), and holds that blank face 6 f before the window opens. Keep text out until the window has filled; the next scene's labels rise in as the border clears.
- **Timing:** Lead-in: converge 22 f, cube turn 12 f, blank hold 6 f. Portal: 39 f at ×1.084 per frame (border gone by about frame 30, inner window edges ≤ 78 px/f). Aspect 1 → 1.78 over the first 30 f. Next-scene labels start from about frame 30 on a 4-6 f stagger.
- **Use when:** The film's energy peak and act break, going inside the product, when the mark or app icon is a tile.
- **Avoid when:** The accent has already flooded the frame once (the tile border is a brief accent flood), or another zoom-through sits in the same act.

### Scale-through cut

`tr-scale-through-cut` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature, loop

An object shrinks faster and faster toward a fixed point, the film cuts, and a matching object appears much larger on the same point and keeps shrinking as it brakes, so one pull-back runs through two different worlds. The mirror version swells into the cut and opens on an undersized object that grows.

- **Build:** Choose an anchor screen point and keep both objects centred on it within ±30 px (fixed sx, sy in an anchor-camera Shot, or transform-origin on the anchor). Outgoing: k = lmix(1, 0.75, prog(f, T − 20, T, E.in)), so the last frame shrinks about 7.8%; cut on an act boundary. Incoming: the same subject in a new medium (3D render to flat map, device to flat UI, brand card to product world) with k = lmix(1.8, 1, prog(f, 0, 40, E.out)). Its first frame shrinks about 8.4%, so scale velocity is continuous in log space. For a related mark shown as a frame-filling macro, use k = 1 + (S0 − 1)·0.84^f from S0 = 8-9 and snap to 1 once |1 − k| < 0.01. Push version: the hero swells 1 → 1.22 on E.in over the last 16-24 f while the rest of the frame dims (brightness 1 → 0.6 on a dark stage), and the next shot opens at 0.8 and grows to 1 over 30 f on E.out.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.zoomThrough`
- **Timing:** Exit: 16-24 f on E.in to 0.70-0.80 (last frame −7 to −9% per frame). Cut on a downbeat. Entry: 1.7-2.0x → 1 over 30-40 f on E.out (first frame −8 to −9%), or an 8-9x macro shrinking toward rest ×0.84 per frame and settled by about 30 f. Anchor drift ≤ 30 px. Push variant: +20-25% over 16-24 f, then 0.8 → 1 over 30 f.
- **Use when:** Changing medium or world while keeping the subject: 3D to flat, device to UI, brand card to product, a mark coming back as a macro. Also hero pull-backs at act changes.
- **Avoid when:** The two objects cannot share a centre point, or both sides are calm; a scale jump without matched scale velocity reads as a jump cut. Use it at most twice per film.

### Spin accelerates and the frame empties at peak

`dv-spin-up-into-cut` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, feature

A field of tiles spins faster each frame (x1.15-1.43 a frame) while zooming out; the words are erased one every 2 frames so the frame is text-free at peak spin, the cut lands on the fastest frame and the strongest accent, and the spin decays after.

- **Build:** Build: spinUp(f, { start, cut, from: 0.35, to: 7.25 }) (fx/Orbit): the spin grows by one ratio a frame into the cut on its fastest frame and decays after it with no speed step (rotationDecay from the peak); zoom out on the camera, erase the words on HardStep every 4 f so the frame is empty at the peak. Anatomy: Spin 0.7 -> 14.5 deg/f, zoom x0.90; words erased every 4 f at 60 fps; empty for 6-8 f. Sound: The peak on the strongest accent (a kick); a pop after the cut.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Orbit.spinUp`
- **Timing:** Spin-up 23-30 f; empty 8 f; decay 33 f.
- **Use when:** A galaxy of features or sources, into the next act.
- **Avoid when:** Text left on screen at peak spin.

### Zoom through into what was inside

`cam-crash-zoom-through` · camera · accent · energy high · launch, sting · also `dv-zoom-through-object`

The camera dives into one shape (a letter's counter, a window, a card) faster and faster until it fills the frame, cuts to what was inside, and the inner shot opens still zooming.

- **Build:** const dive = zoomThrough({ from, anchor, start, factor, frames, ease, centre, box, width, height, fps }); cut on dive.cut (the first frame the box covers 99 % of the frame) and open the inner shot with handoffShot(dive, inner, dive.cut - 1, { carry: ['k'] }) so the log-scale speed carries through. hold: 2 posterises the dive on twos.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.zoomThrough`, `lib/handoff.handoffShot`
- **Materials:** The surface reveals its material as the camera arrives: a pearly brushed face with a diagonal highlight band (white, about 250 px, at 25 deg), fine streak grain along the band (3-5 % luminance) and faint warm and green rainbow arcs at about 15 %, a 2 px two-hue split on the edges, then a white-out (luma about 16 % -> 85 %) on the section-change hit. A screen zoomed into shows world-scale scanlines (3 px pitch scaling with the camera) that vanish on the pull-back.
- **Conditions:** the film's one spectral accent
- **Timing:** x8 in 24 f (14-46 f), a constant ratio a frame (E.linear on log scale) or accelerating (E.buildIn); the inner shot settles in 30-40 f.
- **Use when:** A violent spatial jump into the product at the energy peak of a launch film or sting.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films, any second use in the same film, and readable text on either side of the cut.

### Open on a detail, cut out at speed

`cam-punch-out-carry` · camera · signature · energy medium · launch, feature · also `dv-punch-out-cut`

The film opens on a tight crop of the first line, drifting faster and faster; it cuts on its fastest frame to the wide shot, where the world keeps the same speed (so the screen speed drops by the crop) and settles into a drift.

- **Build:** punchOut({ wide, cut, crop, dir, drift, carry, fps }) returns the camera for any frame; .v(f) is the content's screen speed. wide may itself be a moving camera (a reframeChain): the carried offset adds on top. Give drift a floor so the tight shot moves from its first frame.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.punchOut`
- **Timing:** Crop x3 (2.5-3.5); the drift builds on the house launch profile to its cut speed; the wide shot opens at 1.0 x the world speed (0.9-1.1) and decays in two stages to a residual drift.
- **Use when:** The first shot of a film; any cut from a word to the layout around it.
- **Avoid when:** The tight crop cannot frame the whole line (choose a word, or a smaller crop).

### Snap zoom on the fastest frame

`cam-snap-zoom-defocus` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, vertical, feature

A short build eases into a scale jump that happens in ONE frame, soft for that frame only, then the frame lands and sharpens; the jump sits on a hit.

- **Build:** <SnapZoom frame={f} at={hit} to={1.6} defocus flash /> around the content, or snapZoomState(f, props, film).k on your own camera. pre sets the build (frames and the share of the change it covers), land where the jump frame lands, post the landing (ease, or zeta and carry for a damped settle that carries the jump's speed). defocus draws at most two copies at fixed blur levels; flash { gain } lifts only the jump frame, { gain, rise, fall } makes a light swell around it. List declares(props) in src/sync.ts declares().
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom`
- **Timing:** Build 16 f covering 30 % of the log change (normal 3-16 f), jump on the hit, landing 22 f on E.snapOut (4-22 f). Jump x1.1-2.2 in or x0.3-0.6 out. Defocus 4 px@1080 on the jump frame (3-9 px), clearing in 10 f; a softer frame before it at half that. Light swell up to +60 % mean brightness on the jump frame.
- **Use when:** A punchline, a reveal, a number landing, a change of scale that should feel like a cut without being one.
- **Avoid when:** Two snaps within 2 s, or a calm act.

### Whip that carries a copy swap

`cam-whip-copy-swap` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

The camera whips to the next part of the board on a long build and a short brake; on the whip's fastest frame the old line is cut and the new one is already arriving, so the copy changes where the eye cannot hold it.

- **Build:** const move = whip({ from, to, start, frames, ease, fps }); swapAt(move.peak, { fps }) gives, for each frame, whether the old copy shows, whether the new one shows and its opacity. Shape the whip from its speed with whipCurve({ peak, build, brake }): larger build/brake for a sharper, louder whip. dip adds a small zoom-out hop at mid-move, roll a tilt that is taken back by the end. Put the whoosh's peak on move.peak.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.whip`, `lib/camera-moves.whipCurve`, `lib/camera-moves.swapAt`
- **Timing:** Whip 32 f on E.whipBuild (normal 17-94 f), peak speed at 55-62 % of the move (1600 px/s house, up to 3700). New copy from the frame before the peak at 40 % (normal 35-45 %), arriving over about 34 f on E.snapOut; the old copy is cut on the peak, never faded.
- **Use when:** Changing the subject in one breath; two fragments that belong to one sentence.
- **Avoid when:** More than one whip per act, or the board has nothing to whip to (an empty whip is a smear).

### Whip zoom with roll and counter-roll

`dv-whip-zoom-roll` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, feature

The camera whips to a new subject with an accelerating zoom (about x2) and a roll of up to +17-28 deg with motion blur, then counter-rolls past level and settles; a flat grid can tip into a perspective floor this way; a whip-left with a x1.9 zoom lands on the end of a sentence.

- **Build:** whip({ roll, dip }) with the motion-blur pass on the fast frames. Anatomy: Zoom peak 1.078 a frame, roll +2.3 to +5.2 deg/f then a counter-roll to -4.5 deg/f; blur on the fastest frames. Sound: None needed; a kick on the landing.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 36-98 f.
- **Use when:** A big change of subject; flat to 3D.
- **Avoid when:** Roll over about 30 deg; readable text during the whip.

### No hard cuts: every change hides in a camera event

`dv-one-take-film` · pacing and structure · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A whole film with no plain cuts: every scene change rides a cloud dive, a foreground wipe, a whip, a white-out, a zoom-through, a velocity jump or an iris; about 13 sections of 2.7 s each.

- **Build:** One camera function for the film (lib/camera-moves), a seam list where every seam has a declared carrier. Anatomy: A carrier per seam from the transition families; sections 2-3 s. Sound: Transitions on whooshes and swells.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Sections about 160 f each.
- **Use when:** A launch film that should feel like one continuous journey.
- **Avoid when:** Repeating the same carrier twice in a row.
